title: Language and Imagery
welcome_lead: Close read the lexis. Trace metaphors, sound patterns and semantic fields.
meta_desc: Language and imagery in unseen poetry at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You can now move from the page's visible shape into the poem's verbal texture.

concepts.def: A cluster of words sharing related meaning (warfare, light, water) that builds atmosphere.
Figure where one thing is described as another, mapping qualities (life is a journey).
An extended metaphor, often elaborate (Donne's compass in 'A Valediction Forbidding Mourning').
Alliteration, assonance, sibilance — patterns of sound producing texture and meaning.
Word choice — Latinate vs Anglo-Saxon, abstract vs concrete, formal vs colloquial.
Geoffrey Leech's term — features that stand out against the linguistic background, marking emphasis.

walkthroughs.body_html: A poem on love may draw from a semantic field of warfare (arrows, conquest, surrender). Identifying the field is the first step in tracing its argument.
Patterns of sound do interpretive work. Sibilance can soothe or hiss; plosive consonants can punctuate or violence. Always link sound to sense.
Leech's foregrounding asks: what departure from norm grabs attention? An unusual word order, an unexpected register shift, a sudden archaism — these earn attention.
